The Marketplace ​

The Marketplace is how capability moves between Saidi instances. A package is a JSON document describing an agent, a department, a skill, or an MCP server; a registry is a list of those packages; a source is an adapter that turns some upstream catalog into that same shape.

Nothing in a package executes at install time. Packages are JSON, every file inside is a path plus a string, and remote registries only ever index package URLs — so a package can be read in full before anything touches disk.

For the step-by-step install path, see Installing from the Marketplace. This page is what sits underneath it.

The four package kinds ​

KindContainsWhere it lands
agentExactly one agent folder — AGENT.md plus whatever else it shipsA new directory in the agents root
department1–20 agent folders plus a department blockOne directory per member agent
skillOne skill folder, rooted at the folder and containing SKILL.mdskills/<slug>/ on a chosen agent
mcpOne MCP server name plus a runnable stdio/http/sse configThe chosen agent's MCP config

agent and department install standalone. skill and mcp are attachments — they need a target agent, either an existing one or one created as part of the install. See Agents & Departments for why a capability belongs to one specialist rather than to everything.

The package manifest ​

json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "acme/researcher",
  "kind": "agent",
  "name": "Researcher",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Gathers primary sources and writes cited briefs.",
  "author": "Acme",
  "license": "MIT",
  "tags": ["research", "analysis"],
  "agents": [
    { "name": "researcher", "files": [{ "path": "AGENT.md", "content": "…" }] }
  ]
}
FieldRequiredNotes
schemaVersionyesMust be exactly 1
idyes^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{1,100}$. A / makes the leading segment a publisher namespace
kindyesagent | department | skill | mcp
name version descriptionyesTrimmed and length-capped
author licensenoFree text
tagsnoUp to 12, 40 chars each
departmentdepartment only{ name, lead? }; lead must be one of the packaged agents
agentsagent/department[{ name, files: [{ path, content }] }]
skillskill only{ slug, files }
mcpmcp only{ serverName, transport, config }

A registry is thinner — it indexes packages without carrying them:

json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "name": "Saidi Marketplace",
  "packages": [
    { "id": "acme/researcher", "kind": "agent", "name": "Researcher",
      "version": "1.0.0", "description": "…",
      "packageUrl": "https://…/package?id=acme%2Fresearcher&version=1.0.0" }
  ]
}

A registry entry may also carry transport, official, featured, verified, publisher, installCount, ratingAvg, and ratingCount. Entries missing a valid id, kind, name, version, or packageUrl are dropped rather than rejected — a partly malformed registry still lists whatever parsed.

Validation ​

validatePackage() is the single gate. It runs client-side before preview, again in the orchestrator before install, and again server-side on every publish — the hosted service never trusts what a client posts.

GuardRule
Path traversalNo absolute paths, no empty segments, no ..
Forbidden dirs.git, node_modules, .env anywhere in a path
Secret files.env*, secrets.json, credentials.json, id_rsa, *.pem are refused
Per-file size256 KB
Per-agent budget80 files / 1 MB, scaled by member count for a department
Department ceiling8 MB total, whatever the roster size
Agent slug^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$, unique within the package
Skill slug^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,60}$
Required fileEvery agent needs AGENT.md; every skill needs SKILL.md at its root
MCP configMust resolve to a runnable command (stdio) or a url (http/sse)
MCP secretsA live-looking token in env or headers is refused outright — installers supply their own credentials

Passing validation is not the same as being safe, so packageWarnings() produces a separate advisory list shown before install: executable-style content (scripts/…, .sh, .py, binaries), an AGENT.md that requests permission: all, bundled MCP configuration, and for MCP packages the exact command or URL the server will use.

Source adapters ​

The hosted Saidi catalog is the built-in source. Everything else is an adapter that normalises an upstream format into RegistryItem / MarketplacePackage, so the UI never learns a foreign shape and install stays one action.

Source idLabelKindsPulls fromURL scheme
hostedSaidiall fourThe configured registry URLplain http(s)
skillsmpSkillsMPskillskillsmp.com/api/v1/skills/search — metadata plus a GitHub folder URLskillsmp:
mcp-registryMCP Registrymcpregistry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/serversmcp:
glamaGlama MCPmcpglama.ai/api/mcp/v1/serversglama:
githubGitHub URLskill, mcpAny repo, folder, or file URL you pastegithub:

An adapter implements three methods: search() for the grid, owns(packageUrl) to claim a scheme, and resolve(packageUrl) to produce a full installable package.

Three of the five delegate resolution to the same GitHub extractor. SkillsMP and Glama index repositories, not run configurations, so installing one means walking the repo: a folder holding SKILL.md becomes a skill package; a folder holding server.json, mcp.json, or .mcp.json becomes an MCP package, with an npm package mapped to npx -y <name>, pypi to uvx, and oci to docker. Environment variables the registry declares become empty placeholders you fill in yourself.

SkillsMP and Glama are search-first — an empty query returns nothing rather than a default page. GitHub URL import has no search at all; it only resolves what you paste.

All outbound fetches go through an SSRF-guarded helper: every hop is DNS-resolved and re-checked against a private/reserved/link-local/metadata deny list, redirects are followed manually, and credentialed or non-http(s) URLs are refused. Responses are capped at 1.25 MB with a 20-second timeout.

Caching, ingest, and capture ​

Browsing an external source would otherwise hammer it on every keystroke, so three layers of state sit under the marketplace data root:

PathHolds
marketplace-cache/Raw search results and resolved packages. Searches use a 10-minute TTL; a failed fetch falls back to a stale entry, which is also what makes browsing work offline
marketplace-catalog.jsonThe ingested Saidi catalog — items a superadmin surfaced by searching, deduplicated by id
marketplace-pruned.jsonIds proven not installable, so a re-search never resurrects a dead listing
marketplace-packages/Fully captured packages, served as saidi:<id>

When a superadmin searches with two or more characters, the query fans out across every searchable adapter in parallel, results are merged and deduped by id, and the new rows are ingested into the shared catalog. In the background, materializeCatalog() resolves each new item (up to six at a time), pulls every file, revalidates the result under the catalog id, and freezes it into marketplace-packages/. The catalog entry is then repointed at saidi:<id>.

That repointing is the important part. Once captured, a package is self-contained: preview and install serve it from local disk with no external call, so it survives an upstream outage and installs identically for everyone. A resolve failure is triaged — a transient error (rate limit, timeout, network) leaves the live pointer to retry next search, while a definitive one prunes the listing so nobody is shown something they cannot install.

Installing locally ​

POST /api/marketplace/install takes a packageUrl and does the following:

  1. Resolve the payload. A saidi: URL reads the captured package from disk. A scheme-prefixed URL goes through its adapter. Anything else is a plain remote fetch — and that last case is superadmin-only, because it is the SSRF surface.
  2. validatePackage() the result.
  3. Check the caller may install that kind.
  4. Install by kind.

For agent and department, files are written into a staging directory first, each destination path re-checked to make sure it still resolves inside its own agent folder, and only then renamed into place. Overwriting an existing agent goes through a renamed backup, so a failure mid-way never leaves a half-written agent. Without overwrite: true, an existing directory of the same name causes the package to be reported as skipped.

For skill and mcp, the payload attaches to a target agent — named in targetAgent, or created inline via createAgent. If an agent was created for the install and the install then fails, the agent is rolled back. A stdio MCP command is validated before it is written, and cannot be installed at all on the hosted platform, where only http/sse servers are allowed.

Every install appends an InstalledPackage record:

FieldPurpose
id version kindWhat was installed
packageUrlWhere it came from — reused by update
digestSHA-256 of the package JSON
installedAtISO timestamp
agentsThe agent directories created, or the single attach target
targetAgentskill/mcp only
attached{ skillSlug } or { mcpServer } — the precise uninstall handle

The manifest lives at memory/marketplace-installed.json locally, and per-org under the org's memory directory in cloud mode. Update re-installs the recorded id at version=latest with overwrite: true, reusing the recorded target. Uninstall reverses exactly what the record says was added, then drops the record.

The hosted service ​

The catalog runs as a standalone service, deliberately separate from the per-user orchestrator. It shares only catalog.ts — the types and validators — so it never pulls in the agent runtime.

MethodPathPurpose
GET/healthLiveness plus whether sign-in is configured
GET/registryThe index: newest version of each active package. kind, q, sort, limit, offset, featured
GET/packageFull blob for ?id=&version= (latest allowed)
GET/versionsEvery published version of an id, newest first
POST/publishRe-validates, attributes, and namespace-scopes. Sign-in required
POST/publish/deleteA publisher removes their own package or one version
POST/installFire-and-forget install-count bump
GET/POST/reviewsOne review per reporter per package, ratings 1–5
POST/reportAbuse report
POST/auth/device/start · /auth/device/pollGitHub device flow
GET/accountThe signed-in identity for a bearer token
POST/admin/takedownRequires the x-admin-token header

id is passed as a query or body parameter rather than a path segment throughout, because package ids may contain /.

Three rules do the load-bearing work. Versions are immutable — republishing the same id@version with a different digest is rejected, and an identical republish is idempotent, which blocks a silent supply-chain swap. Namespaces are owned — the first signed-in publisher of login/* owns it, saidi is reserved to configured maintainers, and you may only publish under your own GitHub login. Reports accumulate — five reports auto-hide a non-official package pending review, and reporter IPs are stored only as a salted hash.

Rate limits: 600 requests/minute globally, 30 publishes/hour, 60 reviews/hour, 60 reports/hour. Publish bodies are accepted up to 10 MB, above the 8 MB department ceiling to leave room for JSON overhead.

Pointing at a different registry ​

The catalog Saidi ships with is a hosted service, and that is what a new workspace uses. You can point at a different one from Settings → Connections.

A registry URL ending in /registry is treated as a publish-capable API base. Anything else is treated as a static catalogue: it browses and installs normally but cannot be published to. A bare GitHub repo URL is rewritten to the raw marketplace.json on its default branch.

Client-side state — registryUrl, the marketplace session token, the GitHub access token, and the SkillsMP API key — is held per workspace and encrypted at rest, because it includes bearer tokens. See Settings.
